newsitem.title: UK: Islamic group denounces Algerian jail term.
newsitem.headline: Islamic group denounces Algerian jail term.

text.p: A group calling itself the Islamic Information Observatory asked human rights groups on Friday to put pressure on the Algerian government to free an Islamist woman it said was jailed this week for 10 years.
The London-based group, in a fax to an international news agency, said 50-year-old Maghnia Karim was jailed by a military court in Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
It said she was accused of belonging to the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) and trying to undermine the authorities.
No official comment was immediately available from Algerian authorities and there have been no reports of the trial by Algeria's official media.
"The Observatory calls on the international organisations and human rights groups...to support Madame Karim and her children against injustice," the statement said.
Four of Karim's children belonged to the FIS, including one jailed in Morocco in 1994 for 15 years for illegal arms trafficking. Three others have sought asylum in Bulgaria, Germany and Britain.
The FIS was outlawed in Algeria after violence erupted following the cancellation by the authorities in January 1992 of a general election which the Islamist party was poised to win.
More than 50,000 are estimated to have been killed in the subsequent violence.
